title: The Machine of the Kuiper Line
premise: Orsen Coldharbour has spent eleven years alone tending the Kuiper Line seed vault, broadcasting maintenance logs to a colony that stopped answering. When the warship Meridian returns from a deep-space fold experiment with its crew de-aged by decades—including the colony's founder, who is now a child carrying encrypted memories—Orsen becomes the unwilling courier of a message that could end the interplanetary war: proof that both sides descend from the same sabotaged generation ship. Hunted by factions who want the message buried, Orsen must choose between delivering it and protecting the child founder, and in doing so discovers she herself is a printed copy of the founder's lost daughter. The message is delivered at terrible cost; the war ends not in victory but in shared inheritance, and Orsen claims a family assembled from grief, memory, and choice.
about_author: Tamsin Galloway is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obsolete agricultural data before turning to fiction full-time. She writes quiet, character-driven science fiction about the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: Eleven Winters of Static
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. She records her 4,000th log entry in the silent seed vault, tending frozen embryos and talking to the colony that never replies. A routine sensor sweep detects an unscheduled return vector from deep space. The emotional beat is loneliness sharpened into dread—the first sound in years is a warship's engines.

chapters.title: The Meridian Comes Home Young
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The ship docks crewed by children and young adults wearing veterans' faces; the colony's founder, Ada Voss, is now nine years old. The ship's captain, de-aged to twenty-five, recognizes Orsen's name and goes pale. The beat is uncanny wonder curdling into fear as Orsen realizes she knows these people—or they know her.

chapters.title: What the Fold Took
chapters.summary: Captain Reyes's POV. Flashbacks braid with the present: the fold experiment scattered the crew across their own timelines, and Ada volunteered as anchor, compressing a lifetime of memory into a child's mind. The message she carries is fragmented across the crew's restored memories. The beat is guilt—Reyes brought home a miracle that feels like a wound.

chapters.title: A Message Cut Into Pieces
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The crew explains the message can only be reassembled by someone with vault access to the founding archives—and every faction in the war has already launched ships toward the Kuiper Line. Orsen refuses; Ada, eerily adult behind childish eyes, asks for her help by name. The beat is reluctant duty becoming personal when Ada calls her 'Mama' by accident.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Ice
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Orsen and young gunner Sef. Descending into the vault's sealed sublevels, they find the founding generation records—and evidence the colony was sabotaged from within, by both warring governments jointly. The beat is betrayal; the war's origin is an inherited lie, and Orsen realizes why she was placed here alone.

chapters.title: Printed, Not Born
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The archive reveals Orsen is a somatic print of Ada's daughter, grown and stationed here to keep the bloodline's biometric keys valid. Her whole solitary life was an inheritance mechanism. The beat is identity collapse—she rages at Ada, then finds the daughter's own farewell letter hidden in the ice, written before the print was made.

chapters.title: Three Ships on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Faction warships arrive demanding the message; Reyes stalls them while the crew races to finish reconstruction. Sef, the youngest aboard, bonds with Orsen over being made for purposes they didn't choose. The beat is found family crystallizing under siege—they are not crew and caretaker anymore, but kin.

chapters.title: The Child Who Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, rendered through Orsen's observation. Ada completes the message assembly but the strain begins erasing her—adult memories burning out the child. She chooses to finish anyway. The beat is heartbreak and awe: inheritance means carrying what will hurt you, and Ada hands Orsen the completed message like a relay baton across generations.

chapters.title: Broadcast at the End of the Line
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, climax. With faction guns trained on the vault, Orsen uses her biometric key to broadcast the sabotage proof system-wide, while Ada's failing mind recites the final authentication from a child's mouth. Shots are fired; Reyes takes a mortal wound shielding Ada. The beat is sacrifice—the message lands, and the warships go silent mid-attack.

chapters.title: Seeds for the Long Spring
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, resolution. Weeks later, truce delegations arrive at the vault not as conquerors but heirs. Ada, now holding only fragments, chooses to stay with Orsen rather than be restored to power. They plant the first living seeds in thawed soil together. The beat is quiet hope: family is not what you're printed from, but who you keep.
